question: What is the primary medical goal of antenatal care?

options.A: Ensuring a healthy infant and preserving maternal well-being
options.B: Accelerating the natural timeline of fetal bone development
options.C: Eliminating all common discomforts associated with early gestation
options.D: Preventing the necessity of any future surgical interventions

explanation: Antenatal care focuses primarily on achieving safe motherhood by protecting the health of both the mother and the developing baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: Why do structured prenatal programs play a crucial role in resource-limited regions?

options.A: They serve as a primary defense against preventable obstetric tragedies
options.B: They guarantee that labor will occur without any painful contractions
options.C: They replace the standard dietary requirements needed during lactation
options.D: They completely remove the need for skilled birth attendants

explanation: In areas with high maternal mortality, structured antenatal services catch complications early to reduce preventable deaths. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: According to current guidelines, what is the recommended minimum number of antenatal contacts for an uncomplicated pregnancy?
explanation: Current international standards recommend at least eight contacts with healthcare providers throughout an uncomplicated pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h2)

question: When is the ideal time for a pregnant woman to attend her booking antenatal visit?

options.C: During the final month of labor

explanation: An early booking visit in the first trimester establishes accurate gestational dating and sets a baseline for future health screenings. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h2)

question: What is the primary hormonal driver behind smooth muscle relaxation, delayed gastric emptying, and constipation in pregnancy?
explanation: Elevated progesterone levels relax smooth muscle throughout the body, slowing digestion and causing constipation. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h3)

question: A patient at 28 weeks gestation complains of mild shortness of breath during light housework without chest pain or coughing. What explains this finding?

options.A: Increased tidal volume and respiratory minute ventilation
options.B: Severe pathological narrowing of the main bronchial airways
options.C: Complete collapse of the basal lung fields from fluid overload
options.D: An acute infection settling within the lower respiratory tract

explanation: Respiratory adaptations raise minute ventilation, which frequently makes healthy pregnant women feel slightly short of breath. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h3)

question: What does a comprehensive antenatal booking history specifically aim to establish first?

options.A: Accurate risk stratification and baseline health status
options.B: The exact biological sex of the developing fetus
options.C: Immediate scheduling for elective operative delivery

explanation: The initial history helps identify pre-existing risk factors and sets a baseline for monitoring the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h4)

question: Why is screening for sickle cell status particularly emphasized during antenatal history taking in West Africa?

options.A: It is required exclusively for determining the infant's future blood group
options.B: Sickle cell disease completely cures gestational hypertension in the third trimester
options.C: The trait and disease are prevalent and carry significant maternal-fetal risks
options.D: Hemoglobin variants prevent the normal physiological increase in plasma volume

explanation: High regional prevalence of sickle cell gene variants makes early screening vital to prevent crisis and manage anemia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h4)

question: Which parameter must be checked via urinalysis at every single antenatal clinic visit?
explanation: Testing urine for protein and glucose at every visit helps catch pre-eclampsia and gestational diabetes early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h5)

question: Why is early serological screening for infections such as syphilis and HIV critical during antenatal care?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine blood pressure monitoring at later visits
options.B: It guarantees that the mother will experience a completely pain-free labor
options.C: It eliminates the physiological anemia associated with expanding plasma volume
options.D: It allows for prompt interventions to prevent vertical transmission to the baby

explanation: Early detection and treatment of infections like HIV and syphilis significantly reduce the risk of transmission to the fetus. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h5)

question: Which specific micronutrient supplementation is primarily given in early pregnancy to help prevent neural tube defects?
explanation: Folic acid supplementation before conception and during early pregnancy significantly reduces the incidence of neural tube defects. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering intermittent preventive treatment (IPT) with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine during pregnancy in endemic regions?

options.A: To substitute for the daily requirement of elemental iron and folic acid
options.B: To reduce the adverse effects of malaria infection on the mother and fetus
options.C: To completely eliminate the risk of developing gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: To prevent the development of pregnancy-induced hypertension and seizures

explanation: IPT protects pregnant women living in malaria-endemic zones from placental parasitemia and associated complications. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: Which symptom is a classic red flag for severe pre-eclampsia and impending eclamptic seizures?
explanation: Intense headaches and blurred vision are key neurological signs of dangerously elevated blood pressure in pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h7)

question: A patient at 32 weeks gestation reports that she can no longer feel the baby kicking as actively as she did last week. How should the nurse interpret this finding?

options.A: As a normal side effect of starting daily iron and folic acid supplements
options.B: As a sign that the baby has simply fallen into a deep sleep cycle for days
options.C: As a completely normal adaptation to the reduced space in the uterine cavity
options.D: As a critical indicator requiring immediate clinical evaluation for fetal distress

explanation: A decrease in fetal movement is a warning sign of potential compromise that demands prompt assessment. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h7)

question: What is a core component of birth preparedness and complication readiness?

options.A: Arranging reliable emergency transportation and a designated health facility
options.B: Predicting the exact hour and day that spontaneous labor will start
options.C: Purchasing expensive infant formula to replace exclusive breastfeeding
options.D: Securing exemption from all routine laboratory investigations

explanation: Planning logistics such as transport and facility choice prevents dangerous delays during an obstetric emergency. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h8)

question: Why is the identification of a compatible blood donor emphasized during birth preparedness counseling in resource-constrained settings?

options.A: To prevent delays in managing severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: To replace the need for antenatal hemoglobin and blood grouping tests
options.C: To guarantee that the newborn will not develop neonatal jaundice
options.D: To satisfy routine legal requirements for outpatient clinic discharge

explanation: Having a potential blood donor ready saves critical time if life-threatening bleeding occurs during or after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h8)
